simple.meaning: קַנּוֹא (qannôwʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “jealous or angry.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: קַנּוֹא (H7072) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Joshua 24:19, with occurrences in Joshua, Nahum.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to קַנּוֹא (H7072) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in קַנּוֹא (H7072) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: קַנּוֹא (qannôwʼ) / H7072 is traced through Joshua 24:19, Nahum 1:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7072. qanno קַנּוֺא adjective id.; — קַנּוֺא אֵל Josh 24:19 (E) (compare Deut 6:15 above), Nahum 1:2 (|| נֹקֵם ).

occurrences.englishText: Joshua said to the people, “You can’t serve Yahweh, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your disobedience nor your sins.

Yahweh* “Yahweh” is God’s proper Name, sometimes rendered “LORD” (all caps) in other translations. is a jealous God† The Hebrew word rendered “God” is “אֱלֹהִ֑ים” (Elohim). and avenges. Yahweh avenges and is full of wrath. Yahweh takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he maintains wrath against his enemies.
